name: Saint Albert the Great
history: A Dominican friar and bishop who mastered every science of his day, from theology to botany and astronomy, and taught Thomas Aquinas. He is the patron saint of scientists.
meditation: Faith and reason are two wings. Learn one new thing today and thank God for it.
life: Albert was born around 1200 at Lauingen in Swabia and studied at Padua, where he joined the young Order of Preachers. He taught in Dominican houses across Germany and then at Paris and Cologne. Among his students was a large, silent Italian whom the others called the dumb ox; Albert is said to have replied that the ox's bellowing would one day be heard throughout the world. The student was Thomas Aquinas. Albert wrote on almost every subject: Scripture and theology, the works of Aristotle, plants, animals, minerals and the stars, and he valued careful observation. In 1260 he was made bishop of Regensburg and resigned after two years to return to teaching. In old age he defended the teaching of Thomas, who had died before him. He died at Cologne in 1280 and was canonised and named a Doctor of the Church in 1931.
prayerTo: Saint Albert, you studied the works of God with patience and wonder and saw no quarrel between faith and reason. Pray for scientists, teachers and students, that they may seek the truth honestly and humbly. Help me to use my mind in God's service and to give Him thanks for all that I learn. Amen.
penance: Spend half an hour today learning something about the natural world, and end it with a prayer of thanks to the Creator. Give up an hour of idle scrolling to do it.
prayer: O God, Who made blessed Albert, Your Bishop and Doctor, eminent in the submission of human wisdom to divine faith, grant us, we beseech You, so to follow the path of his teaching that we may enjoy perfect light in heaven. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
